views.name: author_canonical
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  author.authorId AS authorId,
  TRIM(author.authorName) AS authorName
FROM author

params.description: Provides a canonical list of authors (one row per authorId) with normalized author names.
params.when_to_use: Look up author display name given an authorId | Build reports or joins that need a single row per author (dimension table for authors) | Compose into queries that aggregate metrics by author without duplicating author rows
params.output_schema: authorId: unique identifier for the author; derived from table column author.authorId | authorName: trimmed/normalized author name string; derived from TRIM(author.authorName) which sources author.authorName
params.metric: No aggregated metrics are defined in this view. All outputs are row-level attributes: authorId = author.authorId, authorName = TRIM(author.authorName)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to fact or other tables on authorId — e.g., join to a publications or sales fact on authorId — safe for using author attributes because this view is one-row-per-author and thus will not duplicate author attributes when joined as a dimension to many-row facts (author_canonical.authorId = fact.authorId). | Do NOT join this view to another one-to-many child of author directly if you intend to preserve a single row per author without re-aggregation — e.g., joining to an author_books table (one author -> many books) will multiply author rows and any measures derived from a single-row expectation. Instead, either: (a) aggregate the child table first (e.g., COUNT(bookId) GROUP BY authorId) and then join the aggregated result to this view on authorId, or (b) perform joins in a query that includes appropriate GROUP BY on authorId to re-collapse duplicates. | Safe to join to other one-row-per-author dimensions (if present) on authorId without re-aggregation because both sides are one-row-per-author. | Since this view contains no aggregated measures, any composition that expects summed or averaged metrics must ensure those metrics are computed from underlying fact tables (aggregated at the desired grain) before joining to author_canonical to avoid accidental duplication.

views.name: paper_writer
views.body_sql:
SELECT writes.paperId AS paperId,
       writes.authorId AS authorId
FROM writes

params.description: The view lists each (paperId, authorId) authorship pairing — i.e., which authors wrote which papers.
params.when_to_use: Find all authors for a given paperId or all papers for a given authorId. | Count distinct authors per paper or distinct papers per author when aggregated on this view. | Serve as the canonical join bridge between papers and authors (one row per authorship) when composing higher-level metrics. | Filter or restrict downstream queries to a subset of paper-author relationships before further aggregation.
params.output_schema: paperId: identifier of the paper — derived from writes.paperId | authorId: identifier of the author — derived from writes.authorId
params.metric: row_count = COUNT(*) -- number of authorship rows (one row per paper-author pair) in the filtered scope | distinct_authors_per_paper = COUNT(DISTINCT authorId) WHEN GROUPED BY paperId | distinct_papers_per_author = COUNT(DISTINCT paperId) WHEN GROUPED BY authorId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a papers dimension/view on paperId — safe because this view is at one row per (paperId, authorId); joining a papers dimension (one row per paperId) will not duplicate these rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to an authors/author_canonical view on authorId — safe because author_canonical is expected to be one row per authorId (canonical author); joining it will not duplicate the authorship rows. | do NOT join this view directly to any table/view that is one-to-many with respect to (paperId, authorId) (for example, a table of paper_revisions or author_awards that can contain multiple rows per paperId or authorId) without first aggregating that table to the same grain, because doing so will multiply this view's rows and thus duplicate counts/metrics. | when composing metrics: if you need sums/counts from a one-to-many child table, aggregate that child table to the (paperId) or (authorId) level (matching the intended grouping) before joining to paper_writer, or perform the aggregation after joining but ensure you group by the original grain (paperId, authorId) to avoid double-counting. | example safe composition patterns: (1) paper_writer JOIN papers ON paper_writer.paperId = papers.paperId; (2) paper_writer JOIN author_canonical ON paper_writer.authorId = author_canonical.authorId. | example unsafe composition pattern: paper_writer JOIN paper_revisions ON paper_writer.paperId = paper_revisions.paperId (if paper_revisions has multiple revisions per paper) — this multiplies rows and must be avoided or corrected by pre-aggregation.

views.name: paper_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId AS paperId,
  p.title AS title,
  p.venueId AS venueId,
  p.year AS year,
  p.journalId AS journalId
FROM paper p

params.description: Provides one-row-per-paper basic metadata (id, title, venue, year, journal).
params.when_to_use: Look up basic metadata for a specific paperId or small set of paperIds. | Display a list of papers with their title, year, venueId, and journalId. | Serve as a stable base (paper-level grain) to join or aggregate author/writer, citation, or topic data at the paper grain.
params.output_schema: paperId: paper.paperId — the unique identifier for the paper; derived directly from the base table column paper.paperId. | title: paper.title — the paper's title; derived directly from the base table column paper.title. | venueId: paper.venueId — identifier for the venue (conference/workshop) where the paper appeared; derived directly from the base table column paper.venueId. | year: paper.year — publication year of the paper; derived directly from the base table column paper.year. | journalId: paper.journalId — identifier for the journal (if applicable) that published the paper; derived directly from the base table column paper.journalId.
params.metric: This view exposes no derived metrics/aggregates. All output columns are direct projections from base columns: paperId = paper.paperId, title = paper.title, venueId = paper.venueId, year = paper.year, journalId = paper.journalId.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension or lookup tables that are one-row-per-key on their key columns. Examples: |  - Join to a venue dimension (venueId -> venue.id) on paper_basic.venueId = venue.id — safe because venue is one-row-per-venue so paper-level rows are not duplicated. |  - Join to a journal dimension (journalId -> journal.id) on paper_basic.journalId = journal.id — safe because journal is one-row-per-journal. |  - Join to other one-row-per-paper views (sibling NORM views keyed by paperId) on paper_basic.paperId = <other>.paperId — safe because both are one-row-per-paper. | Do NOT directly join without aggregation to one-to-many tables/views that list multiple rows per paper, because that would duplicate paper_basic rows and any measures derived at paper grain. Examples to avoid unless you re-aggregate: |  - Do NOT join paper_basic to paper_writer (which is a JOIN view that typically has one row per paper-author) on paperId without first aggregating paper_writer up to paperId (for example, collecting authors into an array or computing author_count by COUNT(*) GROUP BY paperId). Joining directly will multiply paper rows by the number of writers. |  - Do NOT join to citation, topic, or other event/detail tables that are many-rows-per-paper without re-aggregation to the paper grain first, because row multiplication will occur. | If you need metrics from one-to-many children (e.g., author_count, citations_count), compute them with GROUP BY paperId in the child and then JOIN the aggregated result to paper_basic on paperId — this preserves cardinality and keeps measures correct.

views.name: paper_row_level
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId AS paperId,
  p.title AS title,
  p.venueId AS venueId,
  p.journalId AS journalId,
  p.year AS year,
  p.numCiting AS numCiting,
  p.numCitedBy AS numCitedBy
FROM paper p

params.description: Row-level canonical paper information and basic citation counts for each paper (one row per paperId).
params.when_to_use: Fetch basic metadata for a paper (title, venue, journal, year) by paperId or set of paperIds. | Report or filter papers by citation counts (numCiting, numCitedBy) at the paper granularity. | Serve as the base for joining paper-level attributes into higher-level analyses (e.g., author aggregates, venue summaries) when paper-level measures should remain distinct.
params.output_schema: paperId: unique identifier of the paper (derived from table paper.paperId) | title: paper title text (derived from table paper.title) | venueId: identifier of the venue where the paper appeared (derived from table paper.venueId) | journalId: identifier of the journal for the paper (derived from table paper.journalId) | year: publication year of the paper (derived from table paper.year) | numCiting: count of outgoing citations from this paper to other papers (direct column paper.numCiting) | numCitedBy: count of incoming citations from other papers to this paper (direct column paper.numCitedBy)
params.grounded_columns: paper.paperId | paper.title | paper.venueId | paper.journalId | paper.year | paper.numCiting | paper.numCitedBy
params.metric: numCiting = paper.numCiting  -- stored per-paper count of how many other papers this paper cites | numCitedBy = paper.numCitedBy  -- stored per-paper count of how many other papers cite this paper
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_basic on paperId — safe because both views are one-row-per-paperId, so paper-level measures (numCiting, numCitedBy) are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author_canonical only via an aggregated paper->author mapping (for example, join paper_row_level to a pre-aggregated paper_writer_by_paper that is one-row-per-paper) — safe when the join preserves one-row-per-paperId semantics. | do NOT directly join to paper_writer (a one-to-many paper->writer relation) without aggregating first, because joining this row-level paper view to the many side will multiply rows per paper and therefore duplicate/overcount numCiting and numCitedBy. Instead, either (a) aggregate paper_writer to one row per paperId (e.g., count writers, list authors) before joining, or (b) join and then re-aggregate back to paperId-level, recomputing any paper-level metrics appropriately. | do NOT join to any other one-to-many detail table (e.g., citation edges, keywords, or author assignments) without ensuring the join produces at most one row per paperId (via aggregation, DISTINCT ON / row_number filtering, or other de-duplication), because numCiting/numCitedBy are stored at paper granularity and would otherwise be multiplied. | safe composition pattern example: to compute per-author aggregate citations, first join paper_row_level to an aggregated author-paper mapping that is one-row-per (authorId, paperId) or aggregate papers by author after joining, then sum numCitedBy per author. Ensure aggregation is performed on the paper_row_level fields, not by relying on raw joins that expand paper rows.

views.name: paper_authors
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pw.paperId AS paperId,
  a.authorId AS authorId,
  a.authorName AS authorName
FROM paper_writer pw
JOIN author_canonical a ON pw.authorId = a.authorId

params.description: Maps each paper to each of its canonical authors (one row per paperId,authorId) with the author's canonical name.
params.when_to_use: List all authors for a given paper or set of papers | Filter or group papers by authorId or authorName | Join author information onto paper-level facts when building per-author or per-paper reports | Compose further aggregation by author (e.g., count papers per author) using this view as the granular input
params.output_schema: paperId: paper identifier for the paper — derived from paper_writer.paperId | authorId: canonical author identifier for the paper author — derived from author_canonical.authorId (via paper_writer.authorId) | authorName: canonical display name for the author — derived from author_canonical.authorName
params.metric: row_grain = (paperId, authorId)  -- this view is at one row per paperId+authorId (no aggregate columns present) | count_papers_per_author = COUNT(DISTINCT paperId) WHEN AGGREGATING BY authorId  -- must be computed by aggregating this view | count_authors_per_paper = COUNT(DISTINCT authorId) WHEN AGGREGATING BY paperId  -- must be computed by aggregating this view
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_basic (or any paper-level 1:1/one-row-per-paper view) on paperId — safe because paper_basic is one-row-per-paper, so joining paper_basic to this view will produce one row per paper-author and will not duplicate measures inherent to the (paperId,authorId) grain. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author_canonical on authorId — safe because author_canonical is canonical/one-row-per-author, so it does not duplicate rows when re-attaching author attributes (this view already uses author_canonical for authorName). | unsafe join warning: do NOT join this view directly to any table or view that is one-to-many FROM this view's grain (for example, a citations table that has multiple rows per paperId or a affiliations table with multiple rows per author) without first aggregating that other table to the appropriate grain (paperId or authorId) or otherwise deduplicating, because such joins will multiply rows and therefore multiply counts derived from this view. | aggregation recommendation: to produce author-level metrics (e.g., number of papers per author), aggregate this view by authorId and compute COUNT(DISTINCT paperId) or COUNT(*) depending on whether paperId is guaranteed unique per row; to produce paper-level metrics (e.g., number of authors per paper), aggregate by paperId and compute COUNT(DISTINCT authorId) or COUNT(*). | planner note: because the base SQL is an inner join of paper_writer to author_canonical on authorId, this view already filters to authors that exist in author_canonical; if you need outer (preserve paper_writer rows even when canonical author missing), join paper_writer to author_canonical outside this view with LEFT JOIN and handle NULL author attributes explicitly.

views.name: paper_author_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId,
  COUNT(DISTINCT w.authorId) AS author_count,
  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT a.authorName) AS authors_concat
FROM paper p
LEFT JOIN writes w ON p.paperId = w.paperId
LEFT JOIN author a ON w.authorId = a.authorId
GROUP BY p.paperId

params.description: Per-paper aggregate of its distinct authors: number of distinct authors and a concatenated list of distinct author names, one row per paperId.
params.when_to_use: Get the count of distinct authors for each paper (paper-level author cardinality). | Produce a single-row-per-paper authorship summary (for reporting, joining to paper-level facts, or filtering papers by author count). | Compose into larger queries where you need author_count or authors_concat as paper-level measures without re-aggregating author-level writes.
params.output_schema: paperId: identifier of the paper (derived from paper.paperId in the base table referenced in the view). | author_count: integer count of DISTINCT authorId who wrote the paper (derived from COUNT(DISTINCT writes.authorId)). | authors_concat: string of DISTINCT authorName values concatenated (derived from GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT author.authorName)).
params.metric: author_count = COUNT(DISTINCT writes.authorId)  -- distinct count aggregate computed per paperId in the view's GROUP BY | authors_concat = GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT author.authorName)  -- distinct-name concatenation per paperId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_basic (or any other one-row-per-paper view/table such as paper_row_level if that is guaranteed) on paperId — safe because paper_basic is one-row-per-paper, so joining will not multiply this view's measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author_canonical on authorId only if you first explode authors_concat back to one-row-per-author or if you join to author_canonical via an intermediate writes/paper_authors-like one-row-per-author-per-paper dataset; direct join from this aggregated view to author_canonical on authorId is not possible because this view does not expose authorId rows. | Do NOT join this view to one-to-many child tables (for example a citations, keywords, or versions table keyed to paperId) without re-aggregation, because those joins will multiply rows per paper and thereby duplicate the author_count and authors_concat measures. If you need combined metrics (e.g., authors per paper and citations per paper), join at the paperId key but ensure you either: (a) aggregate the child table to one row per paper before joining, or (b) join first and then re-aggregate at paperId to compute correct totals. | Do NOT join this view to paper_authors or writes directly (one-to-many per paper) expecting preserved author_count unless you remove duplicated rows by re-aggregating after the join. The view already embeds aggregation over writes; joining another writes-like relation will create a many-to-many unless the other side is pre-aggregated. | Safe composition pattern examples: (1) SELECT p.paperId, p.title, pac.author_count FROM paper_basic p JOIN paper_author_cohort pac USING (paperId) — safe one-row-per-paper join. (2) To combine with citation counts: join pac to (SELECT paperId, COUNT(*) AS citation_count FROM citations GROUP BY paperId) USING (paperId) — both sides are one-row-per-paper aggregates, so measures are not duplicated. | If you need author-level detail together with these measures (e.g., each author plus the paper's total author_count), join paper_author_cohort to a one-row-per-author-per-paper relation such as paper_authors or writes (joined to author) on paperId, and carry author_count as a stable paper-level attribute (no re-aggregation of author_count).

views.description: Per-paper aggregate of its distinct authors: number of distinct authors and a concatenated list of distinct author names, one row per paperId.

views.name: paper_coauthors_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId,
  COUNT(w.authorId) AS author_count,
  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT w.authorId) AS author_ids_concat,
  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT a.authorName) AS author_names_concat
FROM paper_basic p
LEFT JOIN paper_writer w ON p.paperId = w.paperId
LEFT JOIN author_canonical a ON w.authorId = a.authorId
GROUP BY p.paperId

params.description: Per-paper aggregation of its authors: counts and concatenated author ids and names for each paperId.
params.when_to_use: Get the number of distinct authors for a given paper (paper-level author cardinality). | Return a paper-level list (concat) of authorIds and authorNames for display or downstream joins. | Compose into higher-level aggregations by paper (e.g., join papers to venues or years) without recalculating author counts. | Serve as a base when you need one row per paper with pre-aggregated author metrics to avoid re-aggregating paper_writer repeatedly.
params.output_schema: paperId: the paper identifier — derives from paper_basic.paperId (GROUP BY key). | author_count: count of author occurrences for the paper — derives from COUNT(w.authorId) over paper_writer.authorId (distinctness implied by join and grouping; note SQL uses COUNT(w.authorId) not COUNT(DISTINCT)). | author_ids_concat: comma-separated concatenation of distinct authorId values for the paper — derives from GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT w.authorId). | author_names_concat: comma-separated concatenation of distinct authorName values for the paper — derives from GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT a.authorName).
params.metric: author_count = COUNT(paper_writer.authorId) per paperId (sql aggregate in view). | author_ids_concat = GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT paper_writer.authorId) per paperId (sql aggregate in view). | author_names_concat = GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT author_canonical.authorName) per paperId (sql aggregate in view).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_basic (or any one-row-per-paper view) on paperId — safe because this view is one-row-per-paperId (GROUP BY p.paperId) so measures are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_row_level or other paper-level normalized views keyed by paperId — safe for the same reason (one row per paperId). | do NOT join this view directly to paper_writer (or any other one-to-many child of paper) without re-aggregating, because paper_writer is one-to-many to paper and would duplicate author_count and concatenations, inflating measures. | do NOT join this view directly to paper_authors or other join views that expand authors per paper without first collapsing back to one row per paper (for example, aggregate after the join) because that will multiply rows and duplicate the pre-aggregated counts and concatenations. | When composing with other one-to-many dimensions (for example, paper -> citations, paper -> keywords), either: (a) aggregate the one-to-many relation to one row per paper before joining to this view, or (b) join first and then re-aggregate the resulting combined rows at the paper level. Both ensure author_count remains correct and non-duplicated. | If you need to join by authorId (to get author-level info), do so to author_canonical on authorId, but be aware this view does not expose author-level rows — joining by authorId would require exploding the concatenated lists or joining the base paper_writer table instead to preserve row-level author relationships.

views.name: paper_keyphrases_datasets_venues
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId AS paperId,
  pd.datasetId AS datasetId,
  pk.keyphraseId AS keyphraseId,
  p.venueId AS venueId,
  v.venueName AS venueName,
  p.journalId AS journalId
FROM paper p
LEFT JOIN paperDataset pd ON pd.paperId = p.paperId
LEFT JOIN paperKeyphrase pk ON pk.paperId = p.paperId
LEFT JOIN venue v ON v.venueId = p.venueId

params.description: Rows that associate a paper, a dataset mentioned by that paper, and a keyphrase assigned to that paper, plus the paper's venue and journal identifiers and venue name.
params.when_to_use: Ask which (paper, dataset, keyphrase) combinations exist and what venue/journal that paper was published in. | Filter or aggregate counts of distinct papers/datasets/keyphrases by venue or journal. | Compose with other paper-level or dataset-level views when you need paper→dataset→keyphrase granularity with paper venue context.
params.output_schema: paperId: the paper identifier (derived from table paper.paperId) | datasetId: the dataset identifier associated to the paper (derived from table paperDataset.datasetId) | keyphraseId: the keyphrase identifier associated to the paper (derived from table paperKeyphrase.keyphraseId) | venueId: the venue identifier for the paper (derived from table paper.venueId) | venueName: the human-readable name of the venue (derived from table venue.venueName joined via venue.venueId = paper.venueId) | journalId: the journal identifier recorded on the paper (derived from table paper.journalId)
params.grounded_columns: paper.paperId | paper.venueId | paper.journalId | paperDataset.paperId | paperDataset.datasetId | paperKeyphrase.paperId | paperKeyphrase.keyphraseId | venue.venueId | venue.venueName
params.metric: This view is purely a normalized/joined row-level view. No aggregate metrics are defined within it. Example derived counts should be computed on top of this view, for example: | distinct_papers = COUNT(DISTINCT paperId) | rows = COUNT(*)  -- counts triples (paperId, datasetId, keyphraseId) | distinct_datasets = COUNT(DISTINCT datasetId) | distinct_keyphrases = COUNT(DISTINCT keyphraseId)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_basic (or other paper-level 1:1 normalized paper views such as paper_row_level or paper_basic_7) on paperId — safe because those views are one-row-per-paper; joining will not duplicate measures that are reported per (paper,dataset,keyphrase) because paper_basic provides at most one row per paper. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to venue (or a venue dimension view) on venueId — safe because venue is one-row-per-venue; attaching venue attributes will not multiply rows. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: aggregate first then join to dataset-level summary views keyed by datasetId — safe when you reduce this view to one row per datasetId before joining, or when the dataset view is one-row-per-dataset and you join on datasetId after appropriate aggregation. | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views such as paperAuthor / paper_authors / paper_writer / paper_coauthors_agg without re-aggregation, because they are many rows per paper and will multiply the (paperId,datasetId,keyphraseId) triples. If you need author-level attributes, either: | - aggregate authors to one row per paper (for example, canonical_author_id per paper) and then join on paperId, or | - group this view up to paperId first (e.g., COUNT(DISTINCT datasetId), COUNT(DISTINCT keyphraseId)) and then join to author-level aggregates. | Do NOT join to another join view that is many-to-many on paperId (for example, a view that expands papers by multiple other entities) unless you plan to re-aggregate this view afterwards; otherwise counts or sums computed from this view will be duplicated. | When composing metrics: if you need counts of unique papers, datasets, or keyphrases, prefer COUNT(DISTINCT ...) on this view rather than SUM over rows, because the base grain is the (paperId, datasetId, keyphraseId) triple. | If you need aggregates at the paper level (one row per paper), perform SELECT paperId, AGG(...) FROM paper_keyphrases_datasets_venues GROUP BY paperId before joining to 1:1 paper-level dimensions to avoid duplication.

views.description: Rows that associate a paper, a dataset mentioned by that paper, and a keyphrase assigned to that paper, plus the paper's venue and journal identifiers and venue name.

views.name: paper_authorship
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pw.paperId AS paperId,
  pw.authorId AS authorId,
  a.authorName AS authorName,
  p.title AS title,
  p.year AS year,
  p.venueId AS venueId,
  p.journalId AS journalId
FROM paper_writer pw
JOIN author_canonical a ON pw.authorId = a.authorId
JOIN paper_basic p ON pw.paperId = p.paperId

params.description: A row-level join of papers to their individual authors providing paper, author, and basic paper metadata for each paper-author pair.
params.when_to_use: List all authors for a given paper or all papers for a given author (author-level or paper-level drilldowns). | Filter or group by paper attributes (title, year, venueId, journalId) while preserving the author identity for each contribution. | Compose downstream aggregations at the paper-author grain (e.g., count authors per paper, count papers per author, co-authorship link building) by starting from a validated one-row-per-(paperId,authorId) base.
params.output_schema: paperId: identifier of the paper — derived from paper_writer.paperId (aliased as paperId in the SELECT). | authorId: identifier of the author for this paper — derived from paper_writer.authorId (aliased as authorId in the SELECT). | authorName: canonical author name for the authorId — derived from author_canonical.authorName (aliased as authorName in the SELECT). | title: paper title — derived from paper_basic.title (aliased as title in the SELECT). | year: publication year of the paper — derived from paper_basic.year (aliased as year in the SELECT). | venueId: identifier of the venue (conference/venue) for the paper — derived from paper_basic.venueId (aliased as venueId in the SELECT). | journalId: identifier of the journal for the paper (if any) — derived from paper_basic.journalId (aliased as journalId in the SELECT).
params.grounded_columns: paper_writer.paperId | paper_writer.authorId | author_canonical.authorName | author_canonical.authorId | paper_basic.paperId | paper_basic.title | paper_basic.year | paper_basic.venueId | paper_basic.journalId
params.metric: row_count = COUNT(1) at (paperId, authorId) grain — implicit identity metric representing one row per paper-author pair. | papers_per_author(authorId) = COUNT(DISTINCT paperId) when aggregated over this view grouped by authorId. | authors_per_paper(paperId) = COUNT(DISTINCT authorId) when aggregated over this view grouped by paperId.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimensional/look-up views/tables on keys that are functionally unique per side to avoid duplicating rows/measures. | Safe: join to author_canonical (or views derived from it) on authorId — author_canonical.authorId is presumed unique (this view already joins author_canonical one-to-one), so measures at (paperId, authorId) are not duplicated. | Safe: join to paper_basic (or views derived from it) on paperId — paper_basic.paperId is presumed unique (this view already joins paper_basic one-to-one), so measures at (paperId, authorId) are not duplicated. | Safe: join to single-row per paper aggregates (e.g., a view aggregated to paperId) on paperId — safe because you are joining two sources that are one-row-per-paper (the paper-level aggregate) and one-row-per-(paperId,authorId); the join preserves one row per (paperId,authorId). | Do NOT join this view directly to any table or view that is one-to-many from paperId or authorId (for example: paper_keyphrases_datasets_venues if it has multiple keyphrases per paper, paper_authors if it is multi-row beyond the same grain, or any row-level table listing multiple entities per paper) without first aggregating that one-to-many side to the paperId or authorId grain. Doing so would multiply rows and therefore multiply COUNT-based metrics (e.g., authors_per_paper) unless you re-aggregate or deduplicate appropriately. | When composing higher-level metrics: derive counts by aggregating this view (e.g., COUNT(DISTINCT paperId) per author) rather than relying on joins to potentially multi-row detail tables. If you must join a one-to-many table, either (a) aggregate the one-to-many table to a single row per join key before joining, or (b) join and then use DISTINCT or COUNT(DISTINCT ...) to avoid inflated counts. | Examples of safe join keys: join on paperId to paper_basic_7 (paper-level normalized view) or on authorId to author_canonical(NORM). Examples of unsafe direct joins: joining to paper_keyphrases_datasets_venues(JOIN) or paper_coauthors_agg(AGG) if those produce multiple rows per paper without aggregation to the paperId or (paperId,authorId) grain first.

JOIN author_canonical a ON pw.authorId = a.authorId

params.description: Provides the canonical author name for each (paperId, authorId) pair — one row per paper author.
params.when_to_use: Look up the display/canonical name of an author for a given paperId and authorId. | Join canonical author names onto paper-level datasets when you need authorName alongside paperId and authorId. | Compose into larger queries that list authors for papers, produce author-level labels, or join to author dimensions without altering counts.
params.output_schema: paperId: unique identifier of the paper — derived from paper_writer.paperId | authorId: unique identifier of the author (as used on the paper) — derived from paper_writer.authorId | authorName: canonical/display name of the author — derived from author_canonical.authorName
params.metric: This view has no aggregated metrics. All columns are direct projections (identity): | paperId = paper_writer.paperId | authorId = paper_writer.authorId | authorName = author_canonical.authorName
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_basic (or other paper-level 1-row-per-paper views) on paperId — safe because paper_basic is one-row-per-paper and this view is one-row-per-(paperId,authorId); joining will not duplicate this view's rows but will expand each paper-author row with paper attributes. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author_canonical (or an author dimension that is one-row-per-author) on authorId — safe because author_canonical is one-row-per-author; this view already uses author_canonical to produce authorName so re-joining to an author dimension on authorId will not duplicate rows. | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views keyed by paperId (for example: paper_keyphrases_datasets_venues, paper_authorship if it is one-to-many per paper, or other per-paper multi-value aggregates) without handling multiplicity (e.g., aggregating the one-to-many side first or deduplicating) — such joins would multiply rows per (paperId,authorId) and therefore multiply any measures derived from this view. | Do NOT join to a coauthor- or affiliation-level table that has multiple rows per (paperId,authorId) (for example, if a table lists multiple roles, affiliations, or keyphrases per author-paper) unless you first aggregate or restrict to a single row per (paperId,authorId), because that would duplicate this view's rows. | Safe composition pattern for building aggregates: if you need per-paper counts of authors, aggregate this view (e.g., COUNT(authorId) GROUP BY paperId) rather than joining this view to another per-paper multi-row table and counting, which could double-count. | If composing measures with other JOIN views: ensure you join this view on the exact keys (paperId, authorId) when combining author-level attributes so the row-level correspondence is preserved; joining on only paperId will expand one author row per paper to multiple rows if the other side is one-to-many by paper.

views.name: paper_author_list
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId AS paperId,
  COUNT(w.authorId) AS author_count,
  GROUP_CONCAT(a.authorName, ', ') AS authors_concat
FROM paper p
LEFT JOIN writes w ON p.paperId = w.paperId
LEFT JOIN author a ON w.authorId = a.authorId
GROUP BY p.paperId

params.description: Per-paper aggregated author summary: number of authors and a concatenated author-name list for each paperId.
params.when_to_use: Return the count of authors for each paper (author_count) when reporting paper-level author metrics. | Produce a readable, comma-separated author list for display alongside paper metadata (authors_concat). | Use as a pre-aggregated building block when composing queries that need one row per paper with its author aggregates (e.g., joining to paper-level metrics or filters). | Filter or rank papers by author_count (e.g., find papers with > N authors) without re-aggregating writes/author tables.
params.output_schema: paperId: unique identifier of the paper; comes directly from paper.paperId (the grouping key). | author_count: integer count of distinct write rows aggregated per paper; derived from COUNT(w.authorId) in the view's SQL (counts rows in writes for the paper; NULL authorId in writes would be counted as NULLs are not included by COUNT). | authors_concat: string of authorName values concatenated with ', ' for the paper; derived from GROUP_CONCAT(a.authorName, ', ') over joined author rows.
params.metric: author_count = COUNT(writes.authorId)  -- paper-level aggregate counting writes rows with a non-NULL authorId per paperId | authors_concat = GROUP_CONCAT(author.authorName, ', ')  -- paper-level string aggregation of authorName values for the paper
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_basic (or any one-row-per-paper view/table) on paperId — safe because paper_author_list is one-row-per-paper (GROUP BY paperId), so measures are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_row_level on paperId only if paper_row_level is guaranteed one-row-per-paperId; safe when that sibling view is normalized to paper grain. | do NOT join directly to writes (or any other one-to-many detail table keyed by paperId, e.g., paper_authorship, paper_authors) without re-aggregating because writes is one-to-many per paper and would multiply author_count and authors_concat. If you must join to such a detail table, first aggregate that table to paperId or re-aggregate after the join. | do NOT join to paper_coauthors_agg or other AGG sibling views on paperId without understanding their grain: joining two aggregated views on the same grain (paperId) is safe; however, joining to an AGG at a finer grain (e.g., coauthor rows per paper) that expands rows would require re-aggregation. | When composing additional metrics that count or sum per paper, either (a) join on paperId to this view and compute new measures separately (ensuring they are also at paper grain), or (b) join this view to dimension tables that are 1:1 with paper (e.g., paper_basic) — these joins will not duplicate author_count because both sides are one-row-per-paper. | If you need author-level detail (one row per author per paper), join back to writes or author on paperId and authorId, but do so at that finer grain and do not treat author_count from this view as additive across resulting rows without dividing or re-aggregating to the paper grain first.

views.description: Per-paper aggregated author summary: number of authors and a concatenated author-name list for each paperId.

views.name: author_id_by_name
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.authorId
FROM author a

params.description: Provides the canonical mapping from author name context to the author identifier (one row per author.authorId).
params.when_to_use: Look up or filter by authorId when you only have an author identity (e.g., join papers to authors by authorId). | Compose queries that need a distinct list of authors as a driving set (e.g., count papers per author after joining to paper tables). | Serve as the single-row-per-author core when building downstream aggregates or joining author-level attributes.
params.output_schema: authorId: unique identifier for an author; sourced directly from table author.authorId
params.metric: authorId = author.authorId (identity passthrough; no aggregation)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a dimension or view that is also one-row-per-author (for example, author_canonical on authorId) using: JOIN author_canonical ac ON author_id_by_name.authorId = ac.authorId — safe because both sides are one-row-per-author and will not duplicate rows or measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper-level tables/views on authorId only when you intend to relate each author to multiple paper rows (e.g., JOIN paper_author_list pal ON author_id_by_name.authorId = pal.authorId). This is safe when you expect the resulting row expansion (one author -> many papers) and will re-aggregate measures at the author granularity afterwards (for example, COUNT(DISTINCT pal.paperId) GROUP BY author_id_by_name.authorId). | do NOT blindly join to one-to-many tables/views (such as paper_authorship, paper_writer, paper_author_list, paper_authors, paper_row_level) without re-aggregation, because those joins will multiply author_id_by_name rows and will therefore duplicate any measures presumed to be author-level. Instead, either: (a) pre-aggregate the many-side (e.g., compute per-author counts in the paper side) and then join, or (b) join and then GROUP BY author_id_by_name.authorId to collapse back to author granularity. | safe to join to sibling NORM views that are one-row-per-entity keyed by authorId; unsafe to join to AGG/SEL/JOIN views that are one-to-many relative to authorId unless the downstream query re-aggregates to re-establish one-row-per-author.

views.description: Provides the canonical mapping from author name context to the author identifier (one row per author.authorId).

views.name: paper_authorship_13
views.body_sql:
SELECT writes.paperId AS paperId,
       writes.authorId AS authorId
FROM writes
WHERE writes.paperId IS NOT NULL
  AND writes.authorId IS NOT NULL

params.description: List of non-null authorship links: which author wrote which paper (one row per paperId × authorId pair).
params.when_to_use: Get all author-paper relationships (who is an author of a given paper). | Filter or join to authorship when building author- or paper-centered results (e.g., attach author attributes to each paper-author pair). | Compose into aggregates that count authors per paper or papers per author by aggregating these rows. | Use as a safe input set for further joins that enrich each (paperId, authorId) pair with additional dimensions.
params.output_schema: paperId: identifier of the paper — derived directly from writes.paperId | authorId: identifier of the author — derived directly from writes.authorId
params.metric: row_count = COUNT(*)  -- counts (paperId, authorId) rows in this view | papers_per_author[authorId] = COUNT(paperId) GROUP BY authorId  -- must be computed by aggregating this view | authors_per_paper[paperId] = COUNT(authorId) GROUP BY paperId  -- must be computed by aggregating this view
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author_canonical (or any author-level 1:1 view) on authorId — safe because this view is one row per (paperId, authorId) and joining to a 1:1 author dimension will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_basic (or any paper-level 1:1 view) on paperId — safe because paper_basic is one row per paperId so measures remain one row per (paperId, authorId). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_row_level (paper-level row) on paperId — safe for same reason as paper_basic. | Do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many views/tables such as paper_keyphrases_datasets_venues or paper_author_names_cohort without first aggregating either side — those are many rows per paper or per author and would multiply rows (and thus any row-level counts) from this view. | If you need to combine with a one-to-many child (e.g., paper_keyphrases_datasets_venues has multiple keyphrases per paper), either: (a) aggregate the child to one row per paperId before joining, or (b) aggregate this view to the desired grain (e.g., papers_per_author or authors_per_paper) after the join, to avoid duplicating counts. | When composing higher-level metrics, always re-aggregate after joining to many-side data: for example, to get distinct paper counts per author after joining paper-level tags, compute COUNT(DISTINCT paperId) GROUP BY authorId rather than SUM(row_count). | This view is at grain ['writes.paperId', 'writes.authorId'] — any join that preserves that uniqueness (i.e., joins to 1:1 dimensions keyed by paperId or authorId) is safe; joins that introduce multiple rows per paperId or authorId are unsafe unless handled via aggregation or distinct.

views.description: List of non-null authorship links: which author wrote which paper (one row per paperId × authorId pair).

views.name: paper_basic_14
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId
FROM paper p

params.description: Provides the canonical set of paper IDs (one row per paper) available in the paper table.
params.when_to_use: When you need a deduplicated list of papers to filter, join, or drive further aggregations. | As the driving (grain) table for queries that calculate paper-level metrics (counts, flags) or join per-paper attributes. | To enforce paper-level scope before joining to many-to-one or many-to-many related data so aggregation and de-duplication are correct.
params.output_schema: paperId: unique identifier for a paper, derived directly from paper.paperId
params.metric: No derived metrics in this view; it exposes the base column paperId = paper.paperId (identity)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension or one-to-one views/tables on paperId — e.g., join to paper_basic (grain paper.paperId) on paperId — safe because both are one-row-per-paper, so this view's rows (and any per-paper measures derived from it) are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_row_level (if it is also one-row-per-paper) on paperId — safe only when that sibling view is guaranteed one-row-per-paper. | do NOT directly join to one-to-many tables/views such as paper_authors (JOIN), paper_coauthors_agg (AGG may be aggregated but check grain), paper_writer (JOIN), paper_keyphrases_datasets_venues (JOIN), or any raw authorship/keywords/venues tables without re-aggregation — joining them directly will multiply rows per paper and duplicate any per-paper measures. Instead, either: | - aggregate the many-side to paper-level first (e.g., compute author_count by COUNT(DISTINCT authorId) grouped by paperId) and then join on paperId, or | - join and then GROUP BY paperId in the outer query to re-derive correct per-paper metrics. | If composing into higher-level aggregations (e.g., total papers per year), this view can be safely used as the distinct paper set to count from (COUNT(DISTINCT paperId) or COUNT(*) when using this view as the driving table).

views.description: Provides the canonical set of paper IDs (one row per paper) available in the paper table.

views.name: paper_authors_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId,
  COUNT(DISTINCT w.authorId) AS num_authors,
  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT a.authorName) AS author_names_concat
FROM paper p
LEFT JOIN writes w ON p.paperId = w.paperId
LEFT JOIN author a ON w.authorId = a.authorId
GROUP BY p.paperId

params.description: Per-paper aggregated author information: number of distinct authors per paper and a concatenated list of distinct author names.
params.when_to_use: Get the count of distinct authors for each paper (paper-level author cardinality). | Retrieve a compact, human-readable list of distinct author names for each paper. | Compose paper-level reports or dashboards where one row per paper is required and author-level details are summarized. | Join into broader paper-level analytics as a pre-aggregated author summary to avoid re-counting or re-concatenating authors.
params.output_schema: paperId: unique identifier of the paper; derived from base table paper.paperId (GROUP BY key). | num_authors: number of distinct authors for the paper; derived as COUNT(DISTINCT writes.authorId) computed over all writes rows that match the paper. | author_names_concat: comma-concatenated distinct author names for the paper; derived from GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT author.authorName) applied to author rows joined via writes.authorId.
params.metric: num_authors = COUNT(DISTINCT writes.authorId)  -- distinct count of writes.authorId per paper.paperId as computed in the view's GROUP BY. | author_names_concat = GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT author.authorName)  -- distinct concatenation of author.authorName per paper.paperId as computed in the view's GROUP BY.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_basic (or any other one-row-per-paper normalized paper view) on paperId — safe because paper_authors_agg has exactly one row per paperId, so its aggregated measures (num_authors, author_names_concat) will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_row_level or paper_basic_7 on paperId only if those are one-row-per-paper; verify that the target is one-row-per-paper before joining to avoid duplication. | unsafe join warning: do NOT directly join this view to any writes-level or author-level one-to-many tables/views (for example writes, paper_authorship, paper_authors, author, paper_author_list, or other author-level JOIN views) on paperId without re-aggregation, because those are one-to-many relative to paperId and will multiply the aggregated measures in this view. | unsafe join warning: avoid joining to sibling AGG or JOIN views that are at finer grain (e.g., paper_author_list which may list each author per paper) unless you first aggregate the finer-grained view back to paperId; otherwise num_authors and author_names_concat will be duplicated across the multiple child rows. | safe composition pattern: if you need author-level detail alongside the aggregates, join paper_authors_agg (one row per paperId) to a derived subquery that aggregates or filters author-level rows back to one row per paperId (e.g., SELECT paperId, some_author_metric FROM ... GROUP BY paperId) — then join on paperId so no duplication occurs. | planner hint: treat paper_authors_agg as pre-aggregated at paperId grain. Any join on paperId to another dataset that is also 1:1 (paperId) preserves counts. Any join to datasets that are 1:many requires re-aggregation (e.g., SUM, MAX, or recompute COUNT(DISTINCT) over the join) to maintain correct metric semantics.

views.description: Per-paper aggregated author information: number of distinct authors per paper and a concatenated list of distinct author names.

views.name: paper_citation_category
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId AS paperId,
  p.numCiting AS numCiting,
  p.numCitedBy AS numCitedBy,
  -- expose raw citation inputs for downstream categorization; keep NULLs as-is
  NULLIF(CAST(p.numCiting AS TEXT), '') || '|' || NULLIF(CAST(p.numCitedBy AS TEXT), '') AS citation_category
FROM paper p
views.description: Per-paper computed citation-category string derived from raw citation counts (keeps raw inputs). The view does not apply external categorization rules here beyond exposing the inputs; downstream logic can map to category strings. This view aggregates at paper level and ensures one row per paper.

views.name: paper_coauthor_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId AS paperId,
  COUNT(DISTINCT pw2.authorId) AS num_coauthors,
  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT pw2.authorId) AS coauthor_ids,
  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT a.authorName) AS coauthor_names
FROM paper AS p
LEFT JOIN writes AS pw1 ON pw1.paperId = p.paperId
LEFT JOIN writes AS pw2 ON pw2.paperId = p.paperId AND pw2.authorId != pw1.authorId
LEFT JOIN author AS a ON a.authorId = pw2.authorId
GROUP BY p.paperId

params.description: Per-paper summary of co-author counts and identity (ids and names) for each paperId.
params.when_to_use: Ask for how many co-authors a paper has (excluding self when multiple writes rows exist). | List or display the co-author ids or names for a given paper. | Compose higher-level analytics that need one-row-per-paper co-author metrics (e.g., join with paper metadata to show title + co-author count). | Filter or aggregate by papers' co-author count when building downstream aggregations (must respect cardinality guidance).
params.output_schema: paperId: the paper identifier for the row — derived from paper.paperId (GROUP BY key). | num_coauthors: number of distinct co-authors on the paper — derived from COUNT(DISTINCT pw2.authorId) over writes rows for the same paperId. | coauthor_ids: comma-concatenated distinct authorId values for co-authors on that paper — derived from GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT pw2.authorId) over writes rows. | coauthor_names: comma-concatenated distinct authorName values for co-authors on that paper — derived from GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT a.authorName) where a.authorId = pw2.authorId.
params.grounded_columns: paper.paperId | writes.authorId (as pw1.authorId) | writes.authorId (as pw2.authorId) | author.authorId | author.authorName
params.metric: num_coauthors = COUNT(DISTINCT pw2.authorId)  -- number of distinct co-author authorId values for the same paperId (computed in the GROUP BY over paper.paperId). | coauthor_ids = GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT pw2.authorId)  -- string aggregation of distinct co-author ids for the paper. | coauthor_names = GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT a.authorName)  -- string aggregation of distinct co-author names for the paper.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_basic (or any one-row-per-paper view/table) on paperId — safe because this view is one-row-per-paper (grouped by paper.paperId), so joining on paperId does NOT duplicate num_coauthors or the concatenated lists. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_row_level on paperId only if paper_row_level is guaranteed one-row-per-paperId (it may or may not be; verify its grain). If paper_row_level is one-row-per-paper, join is safe. | DO NOT join this view directly to any table or view that is one-to-many per paperId (for example: paper_keyphrases_datasets_venues if that expands paper rows into multiple venue/keyword/dataset rows, writes without aggregation, or any per-author/per-keyphrase detail) without re-aggregation because such joins will multiply this view's measures (num_coauthors and the GROUP_CONCAT values) across the many rows, producing inflated counts or duplicated concatenation entries. | If you must combine with a one-to-many detail (e.g., keyphrases or per-author detail), either: (a) aggregate the detail to one row per paperId first and then join on paperId, or (b) join then re-aggregate at the desired grain (paperId) and recompute counts/concats from the joined result. | When joining to an author-level view (one-row-per-author) do so via an intermediate that is one-row-per-paper-author (e.g., paper_authors or paper_writer) and then re-aggregate to paperId; do NOT join this aggregated view to an author-level or paper-author detail view expecting the aggregated measures to remain valid without re-aggregation. | Note on the pw1/pw2 pattern: the SQL uses pw2 filtered by pw2.authorId != pw1.authorId; this ensures co-authors are taken distinct from the specific pw1 row in the join pattern. The result's measures are computed as distinct over pw2.authorId, so joining additional tables that replicate pw2 rows would require re-distincting or re-aggregation to preserve correctness.

views.description: Per-paper summary of co-author counts and identity (ids and names) for each paperId.

views.name: paper_citation_level
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId,
  p.numCitedBy,
  CASE
    WHEN p.numCitedBy IS NULL THEN 'unknown'
    WHEN p.numCitedBy = 0 THEN 'none'
    WHEN p.numCitedBy BETWEEN 1 AND 5 THEN 'low'
    WHEN p.numCitedBy BETWEEN 6 AND 20 THEN 'medium'
    WHEN p.numCitedBy > 20 THEN 'high'
    ELSE 'unknown'
  END AS citation_level
FROM paper AS p

params.description: Classifies each paper into a citation-level bucket (unknown/none/low/medium/high) based on its numCitedBy value; one row per paperId.
params.when_to_use: Get the citation-level label for a specific paper or list of papers. | Aggregate counts of papers by citation_level (e.g., how many papers are high-cited). | Filter/join downstream analyses to only include papers in a particular citation_level prior to further aggregation. | Compose with other per-paper attributes (title, year, venue) when you need citation-level as a dimension.
params.output_schema: paperId: paper.paperId — PK of the paper; grain is one row per paperId. | numCitedBy: paper.numCitedBy — integer (nullable) number of citations the paper has received, taken directly from paper.numCitedBy. | citation_level: derived categorical label — computed via a CASE on paper.numCitedBy producing one of: 'unknown', 'none', 'low', 'medium', 'high'.
params.metric: numCitedBy = direct base column (paper.numCitedBy) — not an aggregate. | citation_level = CASE WHEN paper.numCitedBy IS NULL THEN 'unknown' WHEN paper.numCitedBy = 0 THEN 'none' WHEN paper.numCitedBy BETWEEN 1 AND 5 THEN 'low' WHEN paper.numCitedBy BETWEEN 6 AND 20 THEN 'medium' WHEN paper.numCitedBy > 20 THEN 'high' ELSE 'unknown' END
params.composition: Cardinality-SAFE join guidance: | join to paper_basic (or any other per-paper normalised view such as paper_row_level, paper_basic_7) on paperId — safe because both this view and those are one-row-per-paper, so measures are not duplicated. | join to per-paper attribute JOIN views that preserve one-row-per-paper (e.g., paper_keyphrases_datasets_venues if materialised as one row per paper) on paperId — safe only if that sibling view is also one-row-per-paper. | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many child tables/views without re-aggregation first. Examples of unsafe joins that would duplicate counts: | - Do NOT join to paper_authors, paper_writer, paper_authorship, paper_authors (JOINs) or any author-level/keyword-level/coauthor-level JOINs directly on paperId if those are many-rows-per-paper, because each author/keyword row would multiply this view's per-paper row and thereby duplicate the numCitedBy measure. | - Do NOT join to aggregations that are not grouped back to paperId (or that return multiple rows per paperId) unless you aggregate the child side to one row per paperId before joining. | How to compose safely when combining with one-to-many sources: | - If you need author-level details together with citation_level, first aggregate the one-to-many source to one row per paperId (for example, count_authors_per_paper AS (SELECT paperId, COUNT(*) AS cnt_authors FROM paper_authors GROUP BY paperId)), then join that aggregated result to this view on paperId. | - Alternatively, join this view into a query where the final GROUP BY is at paperId (or higher-level) and use aggregation functions (e.g., MAX(numCitedBy), MIN(numCitedBy), COUNT(DISTINCT paperId)) so that citation measures are not accidentally multiplied. | Planner hints: | - Treat this view as a dimension at paper grain — it provides categorical and raw per-paper citation metrics but not aggregates across papers. | - When building higher-level aggregates (e.g., counts of papers by citation_level per year), perform aggregation at the outer query: GROUP BY year, citation_level COUNT(*) using joins to per-paper year attributes that are one-row-per-paper.

views.description: Classifies each paper into a citation-level bucket (unknown/none/low/medium/high) based on its numCitedBy value; one row per paperId.

views.name: venue_paper_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  v.venueId AS venueId,
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.paperId) AS paper_count
FROM venue v
LEFT JOIN paper p
  ON p.venueId = v.venueId
GROUP BY v.venueId

params.description: Provides the number of distinct papers assigned to each venue (one row per venue).
params.when_to_use: Get the count of distinct papers for a specific venue or set of venues. | Report or visualize papers-per-venue (histogram, ranking, top-N venues by paper count). | Join as a pre-aggregated metric when computing venue-level KPIs (e.g., papers per venue combined with venue attributes). | Compose into higher-level aggregations (e.g., total papers across a subset of venues) without re-scanning the paper table.
params.output_schema: venueId: the unique identifier of the venue, derived from base table venue.venueId | paper_count: the number of distinct papers associated with that venue, derived from COUNT(DISTINCT paper.paperId) in the SQL
params.metric: paper_count = COUNT(DISTINCT paper.paperId)  -- distinct count of paper.paperId for each venue. Computed by left-joining paper to venue and grouping by venue.venueId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to the venue dimension (e.g., the base table/view that is one-row-per-venue) on venueId — safe because this view is one-row-per-venue so its paper_count measure will not be duplicated when joined to another one-row-per-venue dimension. | You can safely join to venue (venue.venueId = venue_paper_counts.venueId) or other venue-level normalized views (one row per venue) without re-aggregation, because key is 1:1 between rows and this view's grain. | Do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many child tables or views keyed by paper (for example paper_row_level, paper_authorship, paper_authors, paper_writer, or any paper-level JOIN/AGG view) without re-aggregating afterwards, because those joins will multiply rows per venue and therefore duplicate the paper_count measure. | If you must combine with a paper-level or author-level table to compute derived metrics, either: (a) aggregate the child data to venueId first (producing one row per venue) and then join to this view on venueId, or (b) join at paper-level and compute the distinct paper count there (do not rely on this pre-aggregated paper_count in that case). | Examples of unsafe joins (will duplicate measures): join to paper_row_level on venueId; join to paper_authorship or paper_authors (author-paper many-to-many) on venueId; join to any view that is many rows per venue. After such joins you must re-aggregate DISTINCT paper.paperId per venue to get a correct paper_count. | Examples of safe joins (preserve measure): join to venue on venueId; join to any other one-row-per-venue normalized view (e.g., a hypothetical venue_profile view keyed by venueId) — in these cases no re-aggregation of paper_count is necessary.

views.description: Provides the number of distinct papers assigned to each venue (one row per venue).

  pw.authorId AS authorId,
  a.authorName AS authorName
FROM paper_writer pw
JOIN author_canonical a ON pw.authorId = a.authorId

params.description: Provides the canonical mapping of which authors wrote which papers and each author's canonical display name (one row per paper-author pair).

params.output_schema: paperId: identifier of the paper (derived from paper_writer.paperId). | authorId: identifier of the author who is listed as a writer on the paper (derived from paper_writer.authorId). | authorName: canonical author display name (derived from author_canonical.authorName).
params.metric: No aggregated metrics are produced by this view; all columns are pass-throughs from base tables. | If used as input to aggregations, derived metrics should be defined at the view's grain (paperId, authorId). Example safe derived metrics to compute on top of this view: papers_per_author = COUNT(DISTINCT paperId) partitioned by authorId; authors_per_paper = COUNT(DISTINCT authorId) partitioned by paperId.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_basic (or any paper-level 1:1 view) on paperId — safe because paper_basic is one-row-per-paper and this view is one-row-per (paperId, authorId); joining will not duplicate the (paperId,authorId) rows and preserves correct composition for aggregations at the (paperId,authorId) grain. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author_canonical on authorId — safe as written (author_canonical is canonical/one-row-per-author), it does not duplicate rows and preserves authorName provenance. | Do NOT join this view directly to a one-to-many child of paper (for example, a citations table, paper_keyphrases, or any other paper-level multi-valued table) without re-aggregation, because such joins will multiply the (paperId,authorId) rows and thus duplicate counts/measures that are computed at the paper-author grain. | Do NOT join this view directly to a one-to-many child of author (for example, author-affiliations history or author_cohort membership when represented as multiple rows) without first aggregating the child to one row per authorId, because those joins will multiply this view's rows for an author and distort author-level metrics. | When composing into higher-level aggregates: if you need metrics at the paper-level (e.g., number of authors per paper), aggregate this view by paperId (e.g., COUNT(DISTINCT authorId) GROUP BY paperId) rather than joining other paper-level one-to-many tables into the view prior to aggregation. | When composing into author-level aggregates: aggregate this view by authorId (e.g., COUNT(DISTINCT paperId) GROUP BY authorId) and only then join to author-level dimensions to avoid duplication. | If you must join to another one-to-many relation and preserve correct counts, perform the aggregation on the one-to-many side first to the same grain (paperId, authorId) or to the target grain, then join. Example safe pattern: (this view) LEFT JOIN (SELECT paperId, COUNT(*) AS kp_count FROM paper_keyphrases GROUP BY paperId) USING (paperId) — safe when the key is paperId and the aggregation is at paper level, but note that this will replicate kp_count across each author row for the same paper; if you want kp_count per paper without replication, aggregate this view first to paper-level before joining kp_count. | Summary rule: this view's grain is (paperId, authorId). Any join that is many-to-one into that grain (many rows in this view to one row in the other table) is safe. Any join that is one-to-many from that grain (i.e., other table has multiple rows per paperId or authorId) will multiply rows and requires pre-aggregation or re-aggregation to avoid incorrect measures.

Do NOT directly join paper_basic_23 to a paper_authors or paper_writer JOIN that contains one row per (paper, author) without re-aggregation, because those are one-to-many from paper -> authors and would duplicate per-paper measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_row_level or other one-row-per-paper normalized views on paperId — safe because paper_basic_23 is one-row-per-paper, so measures (numCiting, numCitedBy) remain unduplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to venue or journal dimension tables (if present) on venueId or journalId — safe because such dims are expected to be one-row-per-venue/journal, so joining preserves one-row-per-paper. | do NOT join without re-aggregation to JOIN/AGG sibling views that are one-to-many from paper (examples: paper_authors, paper_writer, paper_keyphrases_datasets_venues, paper_authorship, paper_coauthors_agg if represented per (paper, coauthor), or paper_author_list) — these will multiply rows per paper and thereby inflate numCiting/numCitedBy unless you aggregate (e.g., SUM(numCiting) is invalid) or first reduce the many-side to one row per paper (e.g., array_agg or count-distinct author_ids). | When composing aggregations: to compute dataset-level or author-level aggregates from paper_basic_23, group by the target key after joining via a one-row-per-paper mapping (for author-level metrics, join through a deduplicated authorship mapping or aggregate paper_author relations to one row per (paper, author) before joining). | If you need to combine this view with a table that legitimately has multiple rows per paper but should not duplicate citation measures (for example: multiple keyphrases or datasets per paper), first aggregate those many-rows into an array or count per paper, then join to paper_basic_23 on paperId — that preserves correct semantics for numCiting/numCitedBy.

params.output_schema: paperId: unique identifier for the paper — sourced from paper_row_level.paperId | title: paper title — sourced from paper_row_level.title | year: publication year of the paper — sourced from paper_row_level.year | venueId: identifier of the venue where the paper was published (conference/meeting) — sourced from paper_row_level.venueId | journalId: identifier of the journal where the paper was published (if any) — sourced from paper_row_level.journalId | numCitedBy: citation count or number of citing works for this paper — sourced from paper_row_level.numCitedBy | distinct_author_count: count of distinct authors associated with this paper (COUNT(DISTINCT pw.authorId)) — derived from paper_writer.authorId

params.metric: distinct_author_count = COUNT(DISTINCT paper_writer.authorId) grouped at paper_row_level.paperId | other output columns are passthroughs (no aggregation) from paper_row_level: paperId, title, year, venueId, journalId, numCitedBy
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_row_level or other one-row-per-paper normalized views/tables on paperId — safe because paper_coauthor_cohort is one-row-per-paper, so measures (distinct_author_count, numCitedBy) will not be duplicated. Example: JOIN paper_basic USING (paperId) or JOIN paper_row_level USING (paperId). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimensional single-row views keyed by venueId or journalId (e.g., venue dimension) on venueId or journalId — safe because those are one-row-per-venue/journal and will not multiply paper rows. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views that list per-author, per-keyphrase, per-dataset, or other repeated rows (for example: paper_writer, paper_authorship, paper_authors, paper_keyphrases_datasets_venues, paper_author_list, paper_author_names_cohort, paper_coauthors_agg) without re-aggregation — joining such one-to-many relations will multiply rows and thus inflate distinct_author_count and other paper-level metrics. | If you must bring in one-to-many detail (authors, keyphrases, datasets) join to an aggregated or deduplicated sibling view that is already grouped to paperId (for example a view that provides counts per paper or a DISTINCT list per paper). If a sibling view is not aggregated, first aggregate on paperId (for example: SELECT paperId, <agg(...)> FROM paper_writer GROUP BY paperId) and then join — this preserves the correctness of distinct_author_count. | When composing higher-level aggregations (e.g., cohort by year, venue), aggregate distinct_author_count appropriately depending on desired semantics: if you need the total distinct authors across a cohort (counting each author once across multiple papers), you cannot simply SUM(distinct_author_count) — instead you must re-derive distinct authors at the cohort grain (e.g., COUNT(DISTINCT authorId) joined from paper_writer filtered to the cohort). SUM(distinct_author_count) is appropriate when you want the sum of per-paper distinct-author counts (authors counted once per paper).

Only join without re-aggregation to views that are guaranteed one-row-per-paper or one-row-per-dataset accordingly; otherwise aggregate those sibling views to a compatible grain before joining. | Safe aggregation patterns: to compute counts of papers per dataset, start from this view and GROUP BY datasetId; to compute counts of datasets per paper, GROUP BY paperId. After such aggregation, you can freely join to one-to-many dimensions because measures have been collapsed to a non-duplicating grain.

FROM paper p

params.description: Per-paper count of distinct datasets associated with each paper (one row per paperId).
params.when_to_use: How many distinct datasets are associated with a given paper (by paperId). | Aggregate summaries of dataset coverage across papers (e.g., distribution, averages) when starting from paper-level granularity. | Joining paper-level dataset counts onto other one-row-per-paper views (to enrich paper records with dataset_count) without changing counts. | Composing higher-level aggregates (e.g., dataset_count per author or per venue) only after correctly aggregating/rolling up this per-paper measure.
params.output_schema: paperId: identifier of the paper — derives from table paper.paperId as selected in the GROUP BY | dataset_count: integer count of distinct datasets linked to that paper — derives from COUNT(DISTINCT paperDataset.datasetId)
params.metric: dataset_count = COUNT(DISTINCT paperDataset.datasetId) grouped by paper.paperId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to any one-row-per-paper dimension/view on paperId (for example: paper_basic.paperId, paper_basic_7.paperId, paper_row_level.paperId) — safe because paper_dataset_counts is one-row-per-paper so joining will not duplicate dataset_count. | Safe to join to JOIN/NORM sibling views that are also one-row-per-paper (e.g., paper_authorship or paper_writer) only if those sibling views are guaranteed to be one row per paper; verify sibling view grain before joining. Joining on paperId to a one-row-per-paper view preserves dataset_count correctly. | DO NOT join directly to one-to-many tables or views on paperId (for example: paperDataset (raw rows), paper_authors (if multi-author rows per paper), paper_author_list, paper_coauthors_agg if it is multi-row per paper) without re-aggregating, because those will multiply rows and thus multiply dataset_count unless you re-aggregate (e.g., SUM(dataset_count) after grouping by the higher-level key or recompute distinct counts at the new grain). | When rolling up dataset_count to a higher grain (e.g., author or venue), compute the higher-level metric as either SUM(dataset_count) only when the datasets are disjoint across papers for that higher grain, or more conservatively compute COUNT(DISTINCT datasetId) by rejoining to the underlying paperDataset table to avoid double-counting datasets that appear on multiple papers for the same author/venue. | If you must join this view to a multi-row-per-paper view, do so in a subquery that aggregates back to paperId (e.g., SELECT paperId, MAX(dataset_count) FROM paper_dataset_counts GROUP BY paperId) to preserve one-row-per-paper before joining. | Explicit example of unsafe join to avoid: joining paper_dataset_counts directly to paperDataset on paperId — unsafe because paperDataset contains one row per (paperId,datasetId) and will duplicate dataset_count for each dataset row.

params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension/lookups that are one-to-one with paperId on paperId — safe because paper_with_basic_metadata has one row per paperId, so joining to another one-row-per-paper relation preserves row cardinality and does not duplicate measures. Example: join to paper_basic (if that view is also one-row-per-paper) ON paper_with_basic_metadata.paperId = paper_basic.paperId. | SAFE to join to single-valued reference tables by key (e.g., venue lookup table keyed by venueId) ON paper_with_basic_metadata.venueId = venue.venueId — safe because venue is one-row-per-venue; this enriches each paper without duplicating paper rows. | Do NOT naively join to one-to-many child tables or aggregate views without re-aggregation (will multiply rows). SELECT

FROM keyphrase k

Doing so would multiply keyphrase_core rows and implicitly multiply any measures assumed to be at keyphrase grain. | Do NOT join to a paper-level JOIN (one-to-many from keyphrase) such as a raw paper-keyphrase association or paper_row_level without re-aggregation, unless the planner/consumer intends to expand keyphrase rows into per-paper rows. | If you need metrics that combine keyphrase attributes with detailed child rows, either (a) aggregate the child rows to keyphraseId before joining, or (b) join and then re-aggregate at keyphraseId to avoid double-counting.

SELECT
  paperId,

params.description: Lists the association links between papers and keyphrases (one row per paperId + keyphraseId pair).
params.when_to_use: Find all keyphrases assigned to a given paper. | Find all papers that contain a given keyphrase. | Count distinct keyphrases per paper or distinct papers per keyphrase when aggregated. | Use as a base set of paper–keyphrase pairs to join to paper, keyphrase, or author-level data (with care to preserve cardinality). | Compose further aggregations (e.g., keyphrase popularity, per-paper keyphrase counts) without double-counting if joins are cardinality-safe.

params.metric: row = 1  -- the view is a straight selection of base table rows; no computed aggregates in the view | distinct_keyphrases_per_paper = COUNT(DISTINCT keyphraseId)  -- can be computed by aggregating this view GROUP BY paperId | distinct_papers_per_keyphrase = COUNT(DISTINCT paperId)  -- can be computed by aggregating this view GROUP BY keyphraseId

If they are one-row-per-author-per-paper, they will increase multiplicity and require re-aggregation. |  | joins that WILL duplicate rows (avoid or re-aggregate): |   - Do NOT blindly join to one-to-many tables/views such as paper_authors (if it is one row per paper-author), paper_coauthors_agg (if it expands rows), paper_keyphrases_datasets_venues (if it associates multiple datasets/venues per paper-keyphrase), or any author-level JOIN that lists multiple authors per paper — joining these will multiply paperId×keyphraseId rows and thus multiply counts derived from this view unless you first aggregate or deduplicate. |  | recommended patterns to preserve correctness: |   - To compute distinct_keyphrases_per_paper: SELECT paperId, COUNT(DISTINCT keyphraseId) FROM paper_keyphrase_link GROUP BY paperId; then join aggregated result to paper_basic on paperId (one-to-one). |   - To compute keyphrase popularity across papers without duplication: aggregate this view by keyphraseId (COUNT(DISTINCT paperId) or COUNT(*) if base ensures uniqueness) before joining to keyphrase metadata. |   - If joining to an author-level one-to-many and you need per-paper keyphrase counts per author, first aggregate per paper in this view, then join to the author-level table and distribute/attribute as required. |  | why these rules hold: the view's grain is strictly [paperId, keyphraseId] (one row per pair as selected from paperKeyphrase). Joining to any table that is one-row-per-paper or one-row-per-keyphrase will preserve that grain; joining to tables that are one-to-many relative to the view's keys will multiply rows and thus any derived counts/metrics unless you re-aggregate after the join.

views.name: paper_coauthor_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId AS paperId,
  COUNT(w.authorId) AS author_count,
  COALESCE(
    GROUP_CONCAT(a.authorName, ', '),
    ''
  ) AS coauthor_names
FROM paper p
LEFT JOIN writes w ON p.paperId = w.paperId
LEFT JOIN author a ON w.authorId = a.authorId
GROUP BY p.paperId

params.description: Per-paper aggregation of how many authors wrote each paper and the concatenated list of their names.
params.when_to_use: Get the number of authors for each paper (author_count) and a string of coauthor names (coauthor_names) for display or downstream aggregation. | Compose higher-level queries that need a single row per paper with pre-aggregated author counts and names (e.g., joining to paper metadata, venue, or keyphrase aggregates). | Filter or rank papers by their author counts or by presence/absence of coauthor names without re-aggregating writes/author tables.
params.output_schema: paperId: the paper primary identifier; derived from table paper.paperId (p.paperId in the view SQL). | author_count: the number of distinct rows in writes associated to the paper as counted by COUNT(w.authorId) in the view; derived from table writes.authorId (COUNT over w.authorId). | coauthor_names: a comma-and-space separated concatenation of author names for that paper; derived from author.authorName (GROUP_CONCAT(a.authorName, ', '), COALESCE to '' when null).
params.metric: author_count = COUNT(writes.authorId)  -- aggregate count of writes rows per paper as expressed in the view SQL | coauthor_names = COALESCE(GROUP_CONCAT(author.authorName, ', '), '')  -- string aggregation of authorName per paper; empty string when no authors
params.composition: Join to paper_basic (or any one-row-per-paper view/table) on paperId — safe because paper_coauthor_counts has exactly one row per paperId (GROUP BY p.paperId), so joining on paperId will not duplicate its measures. | Join to paper_row_level on paperId — safe for the same reason (one-row-per-paper in this view). | Join to normalized paper or paper metadata tables (paper_basic_7, paper_keyphrases_datasets_venues, paper_basic) on paperId — safe; these are typically one-row-per-paper and will not multiply author_count or coauthor_names. | Do NOT directly join to writes (or any other table/view that is one-to-many from paper, e.g., paper_authorship, paper_authors, paper_author_list) without re-aggregation — joining to writes would multiply rows per author and therefore would duplicate/inflate author_count and corrupt coauthor_names unless you re-aggregate (e.g., re-count DISTINCT or re-group after the join). | If you need to enrich with a one-to-many child (e.g., keyphrases, datasets, venues if modeled many-to-many), either (a) join to a pre-aggregated view that is one-row-per-paper, or (b) perform the join and then re-aggregate by paperId (e.g., SUM/COUNT over expressions) to avoid double-counting this view's aggregates. | When composing metrics: treat author_count as a paper-level measure (additive across distinct paperId groups only). Do not SUM(author_count) across rows that duplicate paperId — instead GROUP BY paperId or join only to one-row-per-paper sources. | If combining with other per-paper AGG views (e.g., paper_coauthors_agg, paper_author_list), ensure each is reduced to one row per paperId before joining to avoid multiplicative effects; joining two one-row-per-paper AGG views on paperId is safe.
